# NCM 119: Module 1 — High-Yield Quick Notes & Board Matrix
**Focus**: Rapid-Recall Synthesis, Comparison Matrices, Mnemonics, & Board Trigger Words  
**Exam Targets**: Philippine Nursing Licensure Examination (PNLE) & NCLEX-RN  
**Course Facilitator**: Maila DG. Torres, RM, RN, MAN (Registered Midwife, Registered Nurse, Master of Arts in Nursing)

---

## 1. Master Rapid-Recall Comparison Matrix

### Matrix A: Leadership versus Management
| Dimension | Leadership | Management |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Foundation** | Influence, shared meaning, and vision | Legitimate positional authority and organizational power |
| **Role Type** | Informal or formal (can be exercised by any nurse) | Formally designated and institutionally appointed |
| **Attainment** | **Achieved / Earned** position through trust and skill | **Assigned** position via contract and hierarchy |
| **Responsibility** | Universal duty of every Registered Nurse (RN) | Assigned administrative functions (budgets, hiring, firing, appraisals) |
| **Mindset** | Proactive, independent thinking, challenges the status quo | Reactive/systematic, maintains order, executes protocols |
| **Focus** | People, interpersonal relationships, future horizons | Systems, operational structures, and predictable processes |

---

### Matrix B: Lewin's Three Classical Leadership Styles
| Parameter | Autocratic (Authoritarian) | Democratic (Participative) | Laissez-Faire (Permissive) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Freedom** | Little freedom | Moderate freedom | Maximum / Unrestricted freedom |
| **Control** | High control | Moderate control | Little to no control |
| **Decision-Maker** | Leader alone | Leader and group collaboratively | Group alone or abdicated entirely |
| **Activity Level** | High (commands and inspects) | High (facilitates and coaches) | Minimal (passive observer) |
| **Responsibility** | Assumed by leader alone | Shared across the team | Abdicated / Dispersed |
| **Work Output** | High quantity, good quality | High quality, creative, innovative | Variable, frequently poor quality |
| **Efficiency** | **Very Efficient** (fastest in crises) | Less efficient (deliberative) | Highly Inefficient (drifting) |
| **Best Clinical Use**| **Cardiac Arrest (Code Blue), Mass Casualty** | **Unit Policy & Schedule Revisions** | **Expert CNS / Nurse Researchers** |

---

### Matrix C: McGregor's Theory X vs. Theory Y
| Dimension | Theory X (Authoritarian / Pessimistic) | Theory Y (Developmental / Optimistic) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **View of Human Nature** | Humans inherently dislike work and avoid it. | Work is as natural and rewarding as play or rest. |
| **Core Motivation** | Extrinsic only: money, job security, fear of punishment. | Intrinsic: self-actualization, pride, clinical mastery. |
| **Responsibility** | Workers avoid responsibility and lack ambition. | Workers actively seek and accept responsibility. |
| **Managerial Strategy** | Strict control, constant supervision, punitive write-ups. | Guidance, coaching, autonomy, empowerment, rewards. |
| **Clinical Culture** | Culture of blame, fear, lateral violence, burnout. | Psychological safety, open reporting, shared governance. |

---

### Matrix D: Mintzberg’s 10 Managerial Roles
| Category | Role | High-Yield Clinical Nursing Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Interpersonal** | **Figurehead** | Presiding over a departmental nursing pinning ceremony or nurse retirement. |
| | **Leader** | Onboarding, mentoring, appraising, and motivating clinical staff. |
| | **Liaison** | Coordinating with Pharmacy, Laboratory, and Dietary for patient throughput. |
| **Informational** | **Monitor** | Reviewing monthly medication administration error reports and infection logs. |
| | **Disseminator** | Sharing newly updated hospital isolation precautions during shift huddle. |
| | **Spokesperson** | Presenting unit quality metrics to the Hospital Board or external surveyors. |
| **Decisional** | **Entrepreneur** | Piloting an innovative electronic barcode medication scanning workflow. |
| | **Disturbance Handler**| Intervening immediately in a physical or verbal dispute between staff. |
| | **Resource Allocator**| Setting the nurse-to-patient staffing ratio and ordering medical supplies. |
| | **Negotiator** | Resolving weekend shift coverage trades between two staff nurses. |

## 2. High-Yield Board Mnemonics

### Mnemonic 1: Bennis's 4 Pillars of Leadership — "ATMS"
- **A** - **A**ttention (Management of Attention via compelling vision)
- **T** - **T**rust (Management of Trust through ethical constancy and reliability)
- **M** - **M**eaning (Management of Meaning through clear communication and storytelling)
- **S** - **S**elf (Management of Self through self-awareness and accepting feedback)

### Mnemonic 2: Fayol's Core Management Functions — "POSDC"
- **P** - **P**lanning (Forecasting future needs and establishing protocols)
- **O** - **O**rganizing (Designing unit structure and distributing tasks)
- **S** - **S**taffing (Recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and scheduling nurses)
- **D** - **D**irecting / Leading (Guiding, coaching, delegating, and motivating)
- **C** - **C**ontrolling / Evaluating (Auditing clinical performance and quality standards)

### Mnemonic 3: Emotional Intelligence (Goleman) — "SO-MES"
- **S** - **S**elf-Awareness (Knowing one's emotions and triggers)
- **O** - **O**rganizational Social Skills (Building networks and resolving disputes)
- **M** - **M**otivation (Internal drive for nursing excellence)
- **E** - **E**mpathy (Sensing unspoken concerns and validating feelings)
- **S** - **S**elf-Regulation (Controlling impulses and composure under pressure)

### Mnemonic 4: Hersey & Blanchard Follower Readiness — "R1 to R4 Matching"
- **R1** (Unable + Unwilling/Insecure) $\rightarrow$ **Telling / Directing** (High Task, Low Relationship)
- **R2** (Unable + Willing/Confident) $\rightarrow$ **Selling / Coaching** (High Task, High Relationship)
- **R3** (Able + Unwilling/Hesitant) $\rightarrow$ **Participating / Supporting** (Low Task, High Relationship)
- **R4** (Able + Willing/Confident) $\rightarrow$ **Delegating** (Low Task, Low Relationship)

## 3. Board Trigger Words & Clinical Exam Rules

| If the Exam Question Describes... | The Correct Board Answer / Concept is... |
| :--- | :--- |
| Sudden cardiac arrest, disaster triage, code situation, urgent immediate execution | **Autocratic / Authoritarian Leadership** |
| Long-term policy revision, developing unit vacation guidelines, staff buy-in | **Democratic / Participative Leadership** |
| Independent expert nurse researchers, Clinical Nurse Specialists, seasoned NPs | **Laissez-Faire Leadership** |
| Charismatic vision, higher-order moral values, intellectual stimulation, 4 I's | **Transformational Leadership** |
| Quid pro quo, contingent financial reward, management-by-exception | **Transactional Leadership** |
| Choosing to serve first and lead second, people-centered, meeting staff needs | **Servant Leadership** |
| High critical thinking combined with high active engagement | **Exemplary / Star Follower** (Kelley) |
| High critical thinking combined with passive/cynical engagement | **Alienated Follower** (Kelley) |
| Blind obedience without independent critical thinking | **Conformist / "Yes-Person"** (Kelley) |
| Salary, working conditions, company policies (prevent dissatisfaction only) | **Herzberg’s Hygiene Factors** (Extrinsic) |
| Achievement, recognition, autonomy, the work itself (produce satisfaction) | **Herzberg’s Motivators** (Intrinsic) |
| Time-and-motion studies, assembly line efficiency, standardized equipment | **Taylor’s Scientific Management** |
| Belief that nurses naturally dislike work and must be threatened/controlled | **McGregor’s Theory X** |
| Belief that nurses are self-directed and seek responsibility | **McGregor’s Theory Y** |
| Managing budgets, supply chain, clinical protocols, and staff appraisal | **Nursing Management** (Positional Role) |
| Consciously collaborating with one's supervisor for mutual organizational success | **"Managing Up"** |
| Manager who never leaves the private office and is detached from staff reality | **Emotionally Remote Manager** |
| Manager who seeks trivial flaws to publicly humiliate staff | **Purely Mean Manager** |
| Manager who approves every conflicting request to be liked, draining budgets | **Overly Nice Manager** |
| Manager paralyzed by decisions, treating slackers and stars equally | **Afraid to Decide Manager** |
